plan.title: AD lesional vs control Hallmark GSEA (Python)
plan.analytical_narrative: The DE step is already complete: de_results.csv holds the DESeq2 Wald test for the atopic dermatitis lesional (treated) vs control contrast on 12,000 genes across 6 vs 6 skin samples. The research question asks which Hallmark pathways are enriched in this comparison, so the plan starts directly from de_results.csv rather than re-running DE. Per the grounded procedure (fgsea-equivalent preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, R-0048/R-0107/R-0099), step 1 loads the DE table, builds a full ranked list (every tested gene, ranked by the DESeq2 'stat' column — chosen over shrunken LFC or signed -log10(p) per the disputed rule R-0108, because 'stat' already scales the effect by its standard error and needs no fold-change shrinkage post-processing), and runs gseapy.prerank against the locally staged MSigDB Hallmark human gene set (50 sets, HGNC symbols matching the gene-symbol-indexed count/DE tables) with min_size=15, max_size=500, 1000 permutations, seed fixed for reproducibility. Because gseapy's fgsea-style algorithm reads gene symbols directly and the DE table already carries HGNC gene symbols matching the GMT identifier space, no separate Entrez ID-mapping step is required for this collection; the unmapped-gene share is reported directly as the join failure rate against the Hallmark gene universe. Step 2 repeats the same preranked test against the locally staged Reactome human pathway gene sets as the standard follow-up collection, resolving the Homo sapiens subset via the Reactome pathway index before running GSEA, to see whether Hallmark hits resolve to specific curated pathways. Step 3 produces the report: collapses redundant leading-edge overlaps among significant Hallmark sets, lists leading-edge genes per significant set, compares Hallmark vs Reactome results, and records the full reproducibility record (package versions, seed, gene set collection versions, rank metric, universe, size window) as required by the grounded reporting rules. All scripts are Python only, per the user's explicit constraint.
